title: 15: IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2 Screenshot Fidelity Test
subtitle: Screenshot-grounded interactive test covering project creation, editor completion, execution, packages, refactoring, tab management, navigation, and responsive layout.

steps.title: Show the IntelliJ IDEA welcome screen
steps.why: Start from the same first-run surface shown in the reference screenshot. The left navigation, central welcome message, and New Project, Open, and Clone Repository actions should be visible before any project workspace exists.

steps.title: Open the Java New Project wizard
steps.why: Move from the welcome surface into the Java project-creation dialog. The dialog should expose the technology list, project name and location, build-system choices, JDK selector, sample-code option, and Create/Cancel controls in the same structural layout as the reference.

steps.title: Inspect the detected JDK list
steps.why: Open the JDK selector before creating the project. The menu should distinguish download/add-from-disk actions from detected SDKs and visibly list Java 21, Java 17, and Java 8 installations.

steps.title: Create App_1 and inspect the main IDE skeleton
steps.why: Enter the normal IntelliJ workspace after project creation. The Project tool window should show the project root, .idea, src, .gitignore, External Libraries, and Scratches and Consoles while the editor remains ready for the first source file.

steps.title: Open the src New context menu
steps.why: Use the Project tool window as the source of file creation. The context menu should expose New together with Java Class, Package, File, refactoring, formatting, and search commands instead of jumping directly to a generated class.

steps.title: Open the New Java Class chooser
steps.why: After choosing Java Class, show the focused class-creation popup. The class name and the Class, Interface, Record, Enum, Annotation, and Exception choices should be visible with the same compact IntelliJ popup structure.

steps.title: Create Test.java and open it in the editor
steps.why: Complete the class-creation flow so the project tree, editor tab, gutter, and Java editor all update together. This verifies that the screenshot-matched dialogs are connected to real simulator state rather than being static pictures.

steps.title: Show the editor inspection indicator
steps.why: Add a visible inspection state to the open Java file so the editor can be checked against the reference screenshot for gutter, line highlighting, warning decoration, and status-area behavior.

steps.title: Open Project Structure
steps.why: Open the Project Structure surface using the screenshot-grounded two-column layout. Project Settings and Platform Settings should remain visible on the left while project name, SDK, language level, compiler output, and OK/Cancel/Apply controls appear on the right.

steps.title: Open the Project Structure SDK dropdown
steps.why: Expand the SDK field inside Project Structure and verify the detected Java 21, Java 17, and Java 8 entries together with No SDK, Download JDK, and Add JDK from Disk actions. This is the final visual check for the first screenshot batch.

steps.title: Prepare Test.java with a runnable main method
steps.why: Build the editor state used by the next screenshot batch. The Java file should contain a main method and a simple print statement so completion, execution, refactoring, and navigation features all have a real file to operate on.

steps.title: Show the main-method live-template completion
steps.why: Type toward the Java main entry-point template and show IntelliJ's compact completion row for main(). Clicking the suggestion must insert the main-method skeleton into the active Java class.

steps.title: Show statement completion for sout and related suggestions
steps.why: Open the larger code-completion list around a print statement. The selected sout row and nearby Java keywords and live templates should behave like clickable completion choices, not a static overlay.

steps.title: Run Test and inspect the Run tool window
steps.why: Execute the Java main class and open the Run tool window. The output, process exit status, rerun control, stop state, and hide control should all respond while the editor and project tree remain visible above.

steps.title: Create a package from the Project tool window
steps.why: Open the compact New Package popup over the editor and create a package under src. The text field must accept input and Enter must update the project tree.

steps.title: Open the Move refactoring dialog
steps.why: Show the Move refactoring dialog used to move Java classes between packages. Destination path, search checkboxes, Refactor, Preview, Cancel, browse, and close controls must all be interactive.

steps.title: Inspect Refactoring Preview results
steps.why: Preview a refactoring before applying it. The bottom preview should show a result entry and code context, and its Refactor, Cancel, and close actions must respond.

steps.title: Open the editor-tab context menu and split controls
steps.why: Open the editor-tab context menu and test close variants, split right/down, pinning, copy-path, and related tab actions. Choosing a split option must mutate the editor layout.

steps.title: Show the Java symbol information popup
steps.why: Open the compact symbol information card for a Java class. Package navigation, project identity, edit, and more-actions controls should respond while the editor remains available underneath.
